correctness.rationale: On any strict fused-star proximal cell, soft-thresholding the leaves and solving the strictly monotone hub equation yields an attainable linear slope that averages the hub (mass a) and r fused leaves, while preserving other leaves. All r=0..k cell types occur with strict penalties, for arbitrary independently positive beta_i. Coarea reduces each block induced Gini seminorm to binary cuts. For a cut with fused hub flag c, fused-leaf count A and unfused-leaf count d, the claimed numerator p[d(1-m)+(t-d)m]+d(t-d) and denominator (c+A+d)(n-c-A-d) follow by level-counting, with m=(ac+A)/(a+r). Subtracting the candidate K times denominator is concave in d for K>=1, so d=0,t suffice; complement symmetry, then hub-in/out endpoint optimization give exactly B_r and C_r. The two mass regimes produce max{1,2(k-1)/(k(a+1)),max_r a(r+1)(k-r)/(k(a+r))}. Independent exact-rational cut enumeration matched this formula for 42 combinations of k=2..8 and a in {1/5,3/5,1,7/5,3,10}. The reciprocal interval and five-leaf crossover follow by elementary optimization. This validates the stated two-input real-data bound; numerical examples alone would not.

The published star residual theorem concerns I-F and unweighted hub data, not F with arbitrary hub mass a; its complementary derivative norm and factor near 2 do not imply this fitted-map interval.
